<!--
Use a Conventional Commit PR title: <type>(<optional scope>): <description>

Examples:
  feat(toolsets): add automation tools
  fix(alerts): remove legacy alert routing rule tools [OC-5428]
  docs: clarify MCP client configuration
  chore(deps): update dependencies

Use feat for new features, fix for bug fixes, and ! before the colon for
breaking changes, e.g. feat!: remove a deprecated transport.

Release Please uses commit messages for release notes and version bumps.
When squash-merging, ensure the final commit title follows this format too.
Keep relevant Linear issue IDs as a title suffix, as shown above, and link
the ticket in the description. The title must start with the Conventional
Commit type, not the ticket ID (e.g. avoid [OC-5428] fix(...): ...).
-->

## Description

<!-- What changes are being made? Include any breaking changes or migration steps. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Why is this change needed? Link any relevant Linear tickets. -->

## Testing

<!-- Describe the checks run and their results, or explain why no tests are needed. -->

## Risk Assessment

<!-- Describe any risks and how they are mitigated. -->
